title: Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
9. MOS 2149, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC
I&L

    a. Summary. Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chiefs supervise the
maintenance, repair, and inspection of ground ordnance vehicles and support
equipment. Additionally, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chiefs supervise and
manage the administration of ordnance vehicle related maintenance programs
and facilities. The Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief is technically
proficient in the following areas organizational, maintenance, and resource
management, specifically in the areas of training, records and reporting via
major automated information systems, preventive and corrective maintenance,
equipment availability, publications control, supply support, and the
oversight of command environmental and hazardous waste programs. The Ground
Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief also serves as a Licensing Officer for
Ground Ordnance Maintenance Vehicle Operators and supervises the recovery of
ground ordnance vehicles. The Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief
assists the Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officer in execution of their
duties.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold PMOS 2141, 2146, or 2147.

            (2) Achieve promotion to master sergeant.




                                         3-147                        Enclosure (1)
 3120                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



    c. Requirements. It is highly recommended that the Marine complete the
Ground Ordnance Managers Course (A14GBS6) before promotion to MSgt. However,
non-completion of the course is not a disqualifier from achieving the MOS.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-
1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief, 2181.
common_text: The Ground Ordnance Maintenance OccFld maintains the serviceability of ground ordnance materials. Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

9. MOS 2149, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I&L a. Summary. Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chiefs supervise the maintenance, repair, and inspection of ground ordnance vehicles and support equipment. Additionally, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chiefs supervise and manage the administration of ordnance vehicle related maintenance programs and facilities. The Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief is technically proficient in the following areas organizational, maintenance, and resource management, specifically in the areas of training, records and reporting via major automated information systems, preventive and corrective maintenance, equipment availability, publications control, supply support, and the oversight of command environmental and hazardous waste programs. The Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief also serves as a Licensing Officer for Ground Ordnance Maintenance Vehicle Operators and supervises the recovery of ground ordnance vehicles. The Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief assists the Ground Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officer in execution of their duties. b. Prerequisites (1) Must hold PMOS 2141, 2146, or 2147. (2) Achieve promotion to master sergeant. c. Requirements. It is highly recommended that the Marine complete the Ground Ordnance Managers Course (A14GBS6) before promotion to MSgt. However, non-completion of the course is not a disqualifier from achieving the MOS. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
